name: Tomme [toma]
definition: semi-hard pressed cheese of the Alpine or Pyrenean tomme type, in small wheels with a natural grey rind, mild to earthy (Tomme de Savoie, Tome des Bauges, Toma Piemontese); fresh tomme curd is J3.4.1.08.
notes: Tomme de Savoie sold by US retailer: raw cow milk, grey rind, firm paste

name: Soft thistle-rennet cheese (torta)
definition: sheep's-milk cheese set with thistle (Cynara) rennet and ripened under a firm natural rind until the paste is soft and spoonable (Serra da Estrela, La Serena, Azeitão, Torta del Casar).
notes: Torta del Casar DOP, raw sheep milk, vegetable rennet, creamy; cardo not stated on page

name: Wensleydale
definition: crumbly, moist, mild pressed cow's-milk cheese of the Wensleydale type; Wensleydale Blue is J3.4.9.03.
notes: Plain Wensleydale sold by Wensleydale Creamery: mild, crumbly, honeyed aftertaste

name: Caerphilly
definition: moist, crumbly, lightly pressed cow's-milk cheese of the Caerphilly type, young and mild or ripened with a soft rim.
notes: Gorwydd Caerphilly, crumbly semi-firm, mouldy edible rind; listing contradicts itself on pasteurisation

name: Lancashire
definition: crumbly or creamy pressed cow's-milk cheese of the Lancashire type, made by mixing curds of more than one day.
notes: Tasty Lancashire, moist crumbly; curds from three days combined

name: Cheshire
definition: dense, crumbly, slightly salty pressed cow's-milk cheese of the Cheshire type, white or coloured red.
notes: Waitrose Crumbly Cheshire listing; page gives no description beyond name

name: Gloucester (Double and Single)
definition: smooth, firm pressed cow's-milk cheese of the Gloucester type, Double (full milk, often coloured) or Single (part-skimmed).
notes: Tesco Double Gloucester 400g listing; page gives no description; Single not shown

name: Spiced Dutch cheese (Leyden, nagelkaas)
definition: Dutch-type pressed cheese of partly skimmed milk with cumin or cloves worked into the curd (Leidse kaas, Friese nagelkaas, komijnekaas).
notes: Sold as Leyden Gouda with cumin, Dutch semi-hard cow cheese; cumin; nagelkaas not shown
